title: Switch-Less Dragonfly on Wafers: A Scalable Interconnection Architecture based on Wafer-Scale Integration
problem: High-performance computing interconnection architectures based on high-radix switches limit injection/local performance and introduce significant latency, energy, and cost overhead. Designing scalable interconnection without these costly switches remains a challenge.
motivation: Wafer-scale packaging and high-speed wireline technologies enable direct-connected high-radix interconnection architectures with high-density, low-latency, and high-bandwidth connectivity for future supercomputers.
method: Instead of using expensive switches with many connections (called high-radix switches), this approach builds high-speed communication networks directly into a wafer-scale chip structured according to the Dragonfly topology—a proven network design. The routing uses both shortest-path and longer-path algorithms that are guaranteed to avoid deadlock (where data gets stuck waiting in circles) and only requires one extra virtual channel (a logical communication pathway). By embedding the network directly in the chip itself, it eliminates expensive external switching hardware while maintaining all the performance advantages of the Dragonfly structure.
key_novelty: It replaces expensive high-radix switches (switches with many ports) with communication networks embedded directly in a wafer-scale chip, while maintaining the proven Dragonfly topology structure.
contributions: Switch-Less-Dragonfly-on-Wafers architecture utilizing wafer-scale integration and distributed NoCs to eliminate high-radix switches
Deadlock-free routing algorithms with minimal virtual channel overhead
Outperforms traditional switch-based Dragonfly in both cost and performance metrics
Generalizable approach applicable to other switch-based direct topologies

metrics.other: improved cost and performance compared to switch-based Dragonfly

limitations: Specific scalability limits and design tradeoffs for extremely large systems not discussed.
